claims.explanation: Diphenyleneiodonium is a flavoprotein/NADPH oxidase (NOX) inhibitor that kills cells by blocking ROS-generating enzymes and generating oxidative stress; selectivity likely reflects dependence on NOX/ROS-generating flavoenzymes for survival, with high NOX4 (and related NOX) expression and NRF2/KEAP1 pathway alterations determining sensitivity. Lines with active MAPK/PI3K-driven proliferation and high ROS output (BRAF/NRAS mutant melanoma, squamous carcinomas) are most killed, whereas EGFR-mutant lung lines and low-NOX lines are protected.

features.basis: NOX4 mRNA determines ROS output and DPI inhibits flavoprotein ROS generation
KEAP1-mutant lines have impaired NRF2 degradation and higher basal ROS, increasing dependence on ROS defense
NRF2 activation alters redox balance and can create sensitivity to ROS-modulating agents
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched among most killed and have high ROS/MAPK signaling
NRAS-mutant melanoma/bladder lines appear among most killed, consistent with MAPK-driven ROS dependence
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, NCIH1437) are among least affected
Most killed lines carry TP53 mutations, though this is common and weak alone
PIK3CA-mutant gastric/esophageal lines appear among most killed
PTEN loss appears in several least-affected lines (786O, ZR751, FTC133, KALS1)
NF1-mutant melanoma/thyroid lines appear among most killed, consistent with RAS pathway activation
Annotated DPI target; NOS2 expression may buffer oxidative stress and reduce killing
Annotated DPI target; endothelial NOS expression may modulate ROS/NO balance and protect
